source_text: Quos enim fecit quia voluit, nec condemnat nisi spretus; si cum non spernitur, faciat consecratione meliores; nec detrimentum iustitiae patitur, et munificentia miserationis ornatur.
pass_a_gloss: For those whom he made because he willed, he also does not condemn unless despised; if, when he is not despised, he should make them better by consecration; he neither suffers a loss of justice, and he is adorned by the munificence of pity.

lemmas.lexica: LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin

pass_b_english: He made them because he willed to do so; he condemns them only when he is despised. If, when he is not despised, he makes them better through consecration, he suffers no loss of justice and is adorned by the generosity of his mercy.

choices.why: Julian's forensic virtue that renders to each his own, without fraude or gratia (partiality).
rejected: righteousness (Pauline overlay unless the verse forces it)

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
